title: Nonzero Cube-Superpoly Coefficients from a Tight Degree Bound
summary: The restricted algebraic degree has an upper bound, but whether tightness of that bound forces all basis-indexed coefficient functions to be nonzero remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Let $f_c$ be a cube superpoly with a basis $Q$ and coefficient functions $f_g$ indexed by $g\in Q$. Suppose that $d(Q)$, the upper bound on the algebraic degree of $f_c\big|_{\{g=0\mid g\in Q\}}$, is tight. Determine whether this implies $\forall g\in Q,\ f_g\not\equiv 0$.

scope.domain: Cube-superpoly structure and Boolean-function decomposition in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: The upper bound d(Q) on the restricted algebraic degree is tight.
parameters: f_c: the cube superpoly under study
Q: a basis for f_c and the index set for its coefficient functions
f_g: the coefficient function indexed by an element g of Q
d(Q): the upper bound on the restricted algebraic degree of f_c
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether tightness of d(Q) implies that every coefficient function f_g indexed by Q is not identically zero.

citations.label: Correlation Cube Attacks: From Weak-Key Distinguisher to Key Recovery

progress.summary: The source presents nonvanishing of all indexed coefficient functions under a tight restricted-degree bound as an expectation rather than a proved result.
citation_labels: Meicheng Liu et al., Correlation Cube Attacks: From Weak-Key Distinguisher to Key Recovery
